Title: The College and Its Origin
BodyHtml:
Govt. Haraganga College opened its doors on 18 December 1938, at a time when opportunities for higher education outside Dhaka were scarce. It began with a single act of generosity: Ashutosh Ganguly of Tongibari donated one lakh rupees — a considerable fortune then — so that the young people of Bikrampur would not have to leave home to continue their studies.

He was not alone in the effort. The local advocate Satish Chandra Bhattacharya rallied support among Munshiganj's educationists, and A. H. M. Wajir Ali, then sub-divisional magistrate and later a sub-divisional judge — nephew and son-in-law of Sher-e-Bangla A. K. Fazlul Huq — lent the project the official backing it needed to take root.

Nearly nine decades later the college still stands on College Road in Munshiganj Sadar, and the reason it was founded has not changed: to put a serious education within reach of the people of this region.

Title: The College Today
BodyHtml:
Govt. Haraganga College is a public institution in Munshiganj Sadar teaching at both higher-secondary and degree level, with 16 honours departments and a faculty of more than 80 teachers. Beyond the classroom, students run a range of clubs covering culture, sport, debate and community service.

In its 87 years the college has educated over one hundred thousand students, who have gone on into public service, medicine, engineering, teaching, business, journalism and the arts, at home and abroad. It is that shared history — not a shared graduating year — that this Association exists to keep alive.

College facts are drawn from the institution's official website. For admissions, results, routines and academic notices, please refer to the college directly — this Association is an independent alumni body and does not administer college affairs.

Title: The Association
BodyHtml:
The Govt. Haraganga College Alumni Association (GHCAA) was founded on 29 November 2025 to give the college's graduates a single place to find one another. Its members are known as HARAGANGIAN.

The Association is non-political, non-religious and not-for-profit. It takes no side in party politics and aligns with no religious body; membership is open to every former student of the college without distinction. Its work is philanthropic, and directed at education and culture.

Motto: Sharing Heritage, Aligning Lives, Integrating Networks
ঐতিহ্যের বিনিময়, জীবনের সমন্বয় ও সংহতির সেতুবন্ধন

Every element of the Association's crest carries meaning: the historic building for the college and its heritage, the open book for knowledge and learning, the torch for enlightenment and guidance, the mortarboard for academic achievement, the handshake for fellowship and mutual support among alumni, and the red and gold border with “Est. 2025” for the founding of the Association. The Association's flag is white, signifying peace, harmony, non-violence and purity.

Use of the Association's name, crest, flag or other branding requires prior permission from the Executive Committee.

Title: What We Do
BodyHtml:
In practice, the Association's work falls into four areas — keeping alumni connected, supporting today's students, looking after members in difficulty, and safeguarding the college's history.

  • Connection — maintaining an accurate alumni register and making it easy for members to find and reach one another.
  • Students — supporting the academic development of current students, and offering mentorship, career guidance and introductions to alumni working in their field.
  • Welfare — scholarships and hardship assistance for students and alumni in financial difficulty.
  • Community — educational, cultural, social and sporting events, and philanthropic initiatives that serve the wider Munshiganj community.
  • Heritage — preserving and promoting the history and traditions of the college, and working alongside its administration and teachers.
  • Governance — running the Association itself transparently and accountably, with published accounts and elected officers.
